passages.text: Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again.
passages.sermon:
This passage gives advice about generosity.
\r\nIt tells you to give freely.
\r\nIt says, "Cast your bread upon the waters."
\r\nThis means you should share what you have.
\r\nYou may not see a return right away.
\r\nBut after many days, you will find it again.
\r\nYour generosity will come back to you in the future.
passages.original: שַׁלַּ֥ח לַחְמְךָ֖ עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י הַמָּ֑יִם כִּֽי־ בְרֹ֥ב הַיָּמִ֖ים תִּמְצָאֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Divide your portion among seven, or even eight, for you do not know what disaster may befall the land.
passages.sermon:
This passage gives advice about sharing what you have.
It tells you to divide your portion among seven people.
It also tells you to divide your portion among eight people.
You should do this because you do not know what disaster may come on the earth.
You cannot predict what trouble may happen in the future.
Sharing with many people prepares you for uncertain times.
passages.original: תֶּן־ חֵ֥לֶק לְשִׁבְעָ֖ה וְגַ֣ם לִשְׁמוֹנָ֑ה כִּ֚י לֹ֣א תֵדַ֔ע מַה־ יִּהְיֶ֥ה רָעָ֖ה עַל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: If the clouds are full, they will pour out rain upon the earth; whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where it falls, there it will lie.
passages.sermon:
Clouds can become full of rain.
When clouds are full, they pour rain on the earth.
A tree can fall to the south.
A tree can fall to the north.
Wherever the tree falls, it stays there.
passages.original: אִם־ יִמָּלְא֨וּ הֶעָבִ֥ים גֶּ֙שֶׁם֙ עַל־ הָאָ֣רֶץ יָרִ֔יקוּ וְאִם־ יִפּ֥וֹל עֵ֛ץ בַּדָּר֖וֹם וְאִ֣ם בַּצָּפ֑וֹן מְק֛וֹם שֶׁיִּפּ֥וֹל הָעֵ֖ץ שָׁ֥ם יְהֽוּא׃

passages.text: He who watches the wind will fail to sow, and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap.
passages.sermon:
A person who waits for perfect conditions will not act.
A person who watches the wind will not plant seeds.
A person who studies the clouds will not harvest crops.
If you only look for the right moment, you will miss your chance.
You must act, even when conditions are uncertain.
passages.original: שֹׁמֵ֥ר ר֖וּחַ לֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ע וְרֹאֶ֥ה בֶעָבִ֖ים לֹ֥א יִקְצֽוֹר׃

passages.text: As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.
passages.sermon:
You do not know the path of the wind.
You do not know how bones form in a mother's womb.
God makes all things.
You cannot understand the work of God.
passages.original: כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר אֵֽינְךָ֤ יוֹדֵ֙עַ֙ מַה־ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הָר֔וּחַ כַּעֲצָמִ֖ים בְּבֶ֣טֶן הַמְּלֵאָ֑ה כָּ֗כָה לֹ֤א תֵדַע֙ אֶת־ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה אֶת־ הַכֹּֽל׃

passages.text: Sow your seed in the morning, and do not rest your hands in the evening, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or if both will equally prosper.
passages.sermon:
A person cannot know the future.
God alone knows what will succeed.
Sow your seed in the morning.
Do not let your hands rest in the evening.
You do not know which effort will succeed.
This one may prosper.
That one may prosper.
Both may prosper together.
passages.original: בַּבֹּ֙קֶר֙ זְרַ֣ע אֶת־ זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וְלָעֶ֖רֶב אַל־ תַּנַּ֣ח יָדֶ֑ךָ כִּי֩ אֵֽינְךָ֨ יוֹדֵ֜ע אֵ֣י זֶ֤ה יִכְשָׁר֙ הֲזֶ֣ה אוֹ־ זֶ֔ה וְאִם־ שְׁנֵיהֶ֥ם כְּאֶחָ֖ד טוֹבִֽים׃

passages.text: Light is sweet, and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.
passages.sermon: Light is sweet.\r\nIt is good for the eyes to see the sun.
passages.original: וּמָת֖וֹק הָא֑וֹר וְט֥וֹב לַֽעֵינַ֖יִם לִרְא֥וֹת אֶת־ הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

passages.text: So if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all. But let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. Everything to come is futile.
passages.sermon:
A man may live for many years.
He should rejoice in every year.
He must also remember the days of darkness.
There will be many days of darkness.
Everything that comes after is meaningless.
passages.original: כִּ֣י אִם־ שָׁנִ֥ים הַרְבֵּ֛ה יִחְיֶ֥ה הָאָדָ֖ם בְּכֻלָּ֣ם יִשְׂמָ֑ח וְיִזְכֹּר֙ אֶת־ יְמֵ֣י הַחֹ֔שֶׁךְ כִּֽי־ הַרְבֵּ֥ה יִהְי֖וּ כָּל־ שֶׁבָּ֥א הָֽבֶל׃

passages.text: Rejoice, O young man, while you are young, and let your heart be glad in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes, but know that for all these things God will bring you to judgment.
passages.sermon:
You are a young man.
You are in the days of your youth.
Be glad during your youth.
Let your heart be joyful.
Follow the ways your heart leads you.
Look at what your eyes desire.
But know this.
God will judge you for all these things.
passages.original: שְׂמַ֧ח בָּח֣וּר בְּיַלְדוּתֶ֗יךָ וִֽיטִֽיבְךָ֤ לִבְּךָ֙ בִּימֵ֣י בְחוּרוֹתֶ֔ךָ וְהַלֵּךְ֙ בְּדַרְכֵ֣י לִבְּךָ֔ וּבְמַרְאֵ֖י עֵינֶ֑יךָ וְדָ֕ע כִּ֧י עַל־ כָּל־ אֵ֛לֶּה יְבִֽיאֲךָ֥ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: So banish sorrow from your heart, and cast off pain from your body, for youth and vigor are fleeting.
passages.sermon:
Remove sorrow from your heart.
Remove pain from your body.
Youth does not last.
Vigor passes quickly.
These things are fleeting.
passages.original: וְהָסֵ֥ר כַּ֙עַס֙ מִלִּבֶּ֔ךָ וְהַעֲבֵ֥ר רָעָ֖ה מִבְּשָׂרֶ֑ךָ כִּֽי־ הַיַּלְד֥וּת וְהַֽשַּׁחֲר֖וּת הָֽבֶל׃
